Read one step sheet, finding its header row

Source: R/fiss_parse.R
knw_fiss_read_step.Rd

The header is not row 1: title, instruction and section rows sit above the field labels, and how many depends on the edition and the step (rows 17, 26 and 31 for Step 1, 4 to 23 for the others). The label row is the first within the top 40 whose first non-empty cell starts with "REFERENCE NUMBER". Its labels become janitor::make_clean_names() names, and an edition's variant name is renamed to the canonical one unless the sheet already carries the canonical name. A data row must carry a reference number, which drops the template's pre-formatted blank entry rows.

Usage

knw_fiss_read_step(path, sheet)

Arguments

path

string, a workbook (.xls or .xlsx).

sheet

string, the sheet to read.

Value

A list: status ("ok", "empty_sheet" or "no_header"), header_row, banner (the first non-empty cell of row 1, which names the template edition), rows_raw (rows under the header before filtering) and data (a tibble of the rows kept, every cell as readxl returned it, or NULL).

Examples

f <- system.file("testdata", "fiss", "template_v2.xls", package = "knowledge")
s <- knw_fiss_read_step(f, "Step 1 (Ref. and Loc. Info)")
s$header_row
#> [1] 31
s$banner
#> [1] "Fish Data Submission Spreadsheet Template -V 2.0, April 27, 2012"
s$data[, c("reference_number", "utm_zone", "utm_easting", "utm_northing")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   reference_number utm_zone utm_easting utm_northing
#>   <chr>            <chr>    <chr>       <chr>       
#> 1 1                10       612000      5980000     
#> 2 2                11U      312000      5700000     
#> 3 3                10       613500      5981200     
#> 4 4                NA       NA          NA          
#> 5 5                NA       NA          NA
